title: Resolved: CSS Class Prefix Selector
summary:
Just looking at what Bramus shared the other day:/* Adding a base class */ .btn { padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border-radius: 4px; } /* Listing everything... yuck!
*/ .btn-primary, .btn-secondary, .btn-danger { padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border-radius: 4px; } /* Works, but performs badly */ [class^="btn-"], [class*=" btn-"] { padding: 0.5rem 1rem; } /* Newly resolved class prefix selector */ .btn-* { padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border-radius: 4px; }First off, if you don’t follow Bramus, where have you been?!
Existing substring selectors — class^="prefix" and class=*" prefix" — are verbose and defintely less readable than a simple .prefix-* .
— Brian Kardell (@bkardell.com) 2026-08-20T15:43:02.158ZThen again, I do like how we extended color functions for brevity, like:/* old */ color: hsla(100, 50%, 50%, .5); /* new */ color: hsl(100 50 50% / .5);And it’s backwards-compatible, so no real harm if you continue to use the “old” way.
It’s not like substring selectors don’t have other use cases and become totally obsolete.
